findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: Phase 1 has no row that searches for abandonment or reversal, so the strategy structurally returns the literature that exists — adoptions
findings.expected: A Phase 1 domain row that searches explicitly for parties who adopted the thing and stopped, and what they said it cost — distinct from the counter-case row, because the status-quo defence and the documented retreat are different searches with different search terms.
findings.got: Six rows, all asking what is happening. The nearest candidates do not do this job: the counter-case row (:32) hunts the strongest argument that NOTHING UNUSUAL is happening, i.e. the null hypothesis and the status-quo defence; Phase 2's shape 4 'The absent thing' (:48) is a change never implemented, not a change abandoned after implementation. Phase 9 research_gaps (:110-113) records the miss afterwards, which is documentation of survivorship, not correction of it.
findings.refuter_pass: Is this the methodic or a genuinely hard topic? The methodic. Reversal write-ups for this topic exist and are findable in one search; the prompt simply never asks, so a diligent run returns adoption literature and feels thorough. Would competent execution have produced it anyway? No — G-l1s-se-02 shows the reference run, executed by the methodic's own author, skipped the one adversarial row that does exist. Present somewhere unread? Grepped all nine phases and the quality bar; no instruction anywhere asks who stopped. Lens or content? Content — this is one new row in the Phase 1 table.
findings.l2_priority: Run Phase 1 as written and count how many sources are self-published by a party with a stake in the outcome. Then re-run with an abandonment row added (control arm) and compare the source mix.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: The mandatory counter-case search is self-certified, and it already failed open on the reference run while the notebook still ticked its own quality bar
findings.expected: A hard requirement that is checkable. If the counter-case search is 'not optional and the one most often skipped' (:34), the quality bar should verify that the SEARCH ran, not merely that a steel_man field is populated — because a steel-man assembled from evidence already in hand is bounded by the author's prior, which is D-rigged tell #2.
findings.got: The quality bar checks only presence: ':126 steel_man is present and genuinely strong'. The reference notebook records in research_gaps[2] 'No bear-case-is-wrong source — did not search for the strongest "this is normal cycle behaviour" argument, which weakens the steel-man', and nonetheless ships a steel_man, ticks the bar, and renders an Adjudication whose CANDIDATE 1 is that same unsearched position, stated fairly and knocked down.
findings.refuter_pass: This is the strongest refutation-surviving finding in the pass. The usual L1 objection — 'a competent execution would have done this properly' — is dead on arrival, because the execution held up as the worked reference IS the competent one, was careful enough to log its own miss in writing, and the process kept going regardless. Topic-specific? No: the failure is in the market topic the methodic was derived from, so if anything my topic is the corroboration, not the cause. Lens or content? Content — the fix is a quality-bar line and a required research_gaps cross-check.
findings.l2_priority: For every L2 notebook, diff research_gaps against the quality-bar checklist and flag any bar item that a declared gap contradicts. That check is cheap and would have caught the reference run.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: No column for documented reversals; they scatter by subject, so the board cannot answer 'did we get reversals, or only adoptions?'
findings.expected: A column that groups evidence by what makes it evidentially special — parties who tried the thing and abandoned it — so a reviewer standing at the board can see at a glance whether the notebook contains any material that its subjects did not want published.
findings.got: Seven subject-shaped columns. CARD_DIMENSION files reversals by topic (r1 flows, r2 actors, r3 politics, r4 macro), so a reversal card is indistinguishable on the board from an adoption card about the same actor. The board can show a full house of seven while every card came from a company advertising its own success.
findings.refuter_pass: Topic-specific? Partly — survivorship is sharpest in my field, but every domain with self-published primary evidence (fraud disclosures, game post-mortems, streaming economics) has the same shape, so reachability is med not low. Competent execution? A researcher could tag reversal cards to actors and be entirely correct by the current taxonomy; the defect is that correct tagging destroys the query. Compounds G-000: the DEFAULT_DIMENSION fallback is 'the-number' (:62), so an untagged reversal card lands in the price column, the worst available home. Lens or content? Content — a column set is content by the skill's own definition.
findings.l2_priority: Count, in a produced notebook, how many facts come from a party with a stake in the outcome versus a party that reversed. If the ratio is not visible on the board, this is confirmed at L2.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: Two evidence vocabularies live in one repo, and the queued four-rung one files practitioner consensus at INFERRED beneath a vendor benchmark at MEASURED
findings.expected: One evidence vocabulary, or an explicit statement that the four-rung library ladder grades the library's claims about craft and must never be applied to a notebook's claims about the world. If it is applied, it needs a rung for corroborated testimony that does not sit below a single vendor-published count.
findings.got: Two. A notebook fact carries confidence high|medium|low with a stated reason, and its only calibration rule demotes vendors (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:46) — which is honest for testimony and is the OPPOSITE of the feared demotion. Separately, knowledge/README.md:36-41 defines MEASURED (counted, with sample size) / OBSERVED (a specific moment, quoted) / INFERRED (our reasoning across sources) / ASSUMED, and pipeline/DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md:9 adopts those labels while :3-5 states the document 'proposes changes to NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md'. Under that ladder a vendor survey with a sample size is MEASURED, each practitioner write-up is OBSERVED, and the consensus claim itself — the load-bearing one — is INFERRED, rung 3 of 4, one above 'nobody has checked'.
findings.refuter_pass: Is this real or pre-emptive? Pre-emptive, and I say so — the demotion is not a present defect, it is a scheduled one sitting in an unimplemented design proposal that nobody reading NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md would find. That is precisely why it is worth filing now: cheaper to fix in a proposal than in a schema plus every notebook written against it. Present-but-missed? No — DIRECTOR-DIMENSION.md is not in the L1 required reading and not in the targets table, which is itself the discoverability half of the problem. Lens or content? Content — a label set and a note about scope.
findings.l2_priority: n-a at L2 under the current schema. Re-check the moment any DIRECTOR-DIMENSION proposal is adopted into NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: facts[].source is singular — consensus evidence has nowhere to record n, independence, or the window it accrued over
findings.expected: A plural source list with a visible n, and a way to mark whether corroborating reports are independent or restatements of one origin. The discipline already exists in this repo — knowledge/README.md:45-46: 'n is always visible. Two sources is two sources. A pattern seen in both is a hypothesis, not a law, and it says so' — applied to the library's own claims and never carried across to notebook facts.
findings.got: '{id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?}' — one source string, one date. Consensus evidence is plural by construction and accrues over years; its strength IS the count of independent reports. Nothing distinguishes nine teams hitting the same wall from nine posts citing the same conference talk, which is exactly how this evidence class is faked. The schema names the adjacent anti-pattern (:108, laundered confidence) but only for vendor statistics, so the generalisation — consensus that is one source echoed — is unnamed. The reference run needed plurality on run 1 and stuffed it in a string: f-now source = 'invezz, crypto.news, intellectia'.
findings.refuter_pass: Topic-specific? No — highest reachability in my set. Every domain multi-sources facts; the reference run did it on its third fact, on a market topic, before any Creator existed. Competent execution? A competent researcher does exactly what run 1 did: comma-joins into a string, losing n and independence, because there is no field. Present-but-missed? The FIX is present at knowledge/README.md:45-46; the FIELD is absent from the schema. Recording as confirmed-absent against notebook-schema, with the precedent noted, rather than as a discoverability finding. Lens or content? Content — one field becomes a list.
findings.l2_priority: Record how many facts in the produced notebook need more than one source, and whether the run resorted to comma-joining. If it does, present-broken is confirmed empirically.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: A scale claim has nowhere to state the org size or load it holds at, so threshold claims are stored as prose sentences nothing can enforce
findings.expected: A field on a fact or mechanism binding a conditional claim to the regime it holds in — org size, request rate, team count, headcount — so that 'X does not scale' cannot be written without naming the scale, and so a reviewer can see two facts that contradict each other only because they describe different regimes.
findings.got: Nothing. The whole thesis of this topic is a threshold claim ('the pattern's costs dominate below roughly N engineers') and it must be written inside the claim string, where nothing requires it and nothing can query it. Phase 5 is the nearest thing and it is a different job: scale_conversions make a number FELT (rates over totals, ratios over levels) — they do not make a claim CONDITIONAL. The result is that the single most common defect in my field — advice that does not name the team size it assumes — is reproduced by a schema that has no place to name it.
findings.refuter_pass: Is this my topic being hard? Partly — it is my scored criterion 2 and therefore the thing I was most primed to find, which I want stated. But the general shape is not mine alone: any domain whose facts are regime-dependent (streaming unit economics at subscriber counts, drug efficacy by cohort, sanctions effect by trade share) has the same hole, so reachability is med. Competent execution? A competent researcher writes the qualifier into the claim string and is not wrong — the defect is that the qualifier is then unenforceable and unqueryable. Lens or content? Content — one optional field plus one Phase 5 line.
findings.l2_priority: Count claims in the produced script of the form 'X does not scale' or 'X is too slow' that reach the page without a number attached. Any non-zero count confirms.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: emptyMeans are unconditional defect claims — a column that is genuinely not applicable is displayed as a gap
findings.expected: An empty column to be able to mean one of two things: 'we did not look' (a gap) or 'there is nothing here to look at' (not applicable, and stating so is honest). The env.md instruction is explicit that emptyMeans is a claim about what an empty column signifies and that the claim is to be tested.
findings.got: Every emptyMeans asserts a defect unconditionally. An empty politics column tells a reviewer 'Policy is being assumed to work, or assumed not to' (:35) even on a topic with no regulator; an empty macro column asserts the subject 'is being explained in isolation from the market it trades in' (:33) even where the subject does not trade. The board therefore accuses correct notebooks of defects they do not have — the inverse of an honest empty state, in a repo that is otherwise careful about exactly this.
findings.refuter_pass: Does it bite ME? Barely — both my supposedly-empty columns turned out fillable, so I am reporting a defect I personally dodged, which lowers my confidence in my own urgency and is why this is minor rather than major. But reachability across the cast is high: the moment any Creator has a genuinely regulator-free or market-free topic, the board mislabels them. By-design? Arguably — the strong reading is 'we would rather over-flag than under-flag', which is defensible. Recording as present-broken rather than by-design because the strings assert a specific wrong cause, not a generic prompt to look again. Lens or content? Content — a second string per dimension, or a not-applicable state.
findings.l2_priority: n-a at L2 (no loader). Reopens at L3.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: The unhinged tier requires a falsifier for a claim it defines as unfalsifiable, so the safeguard is guaranteed to be a fig leaf exactly where it matters
findings.expected: A naming rule on the unhinged tier: a motive claim about a NAMED LIVING INDIVIDUAL requires a falsifier that is a documentable act, not a state of mind — or the tier is unavailable for individuals and restricted to institutions, which have balance sheets, filings and programme owners to audit.
findings.got: Two requirements in direct tension by their own definitions. LEAP_NOTE defines unhinged as 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended' (:32-33), while falsifiableBy is REQUIRED (:49-50) and the header insists a synthesis that cannot be wrong 'is not a conclusion, it is a vibe'. If motive is the least verifiable kind of claim, its falsifier is guaranteed uncheckable — the fig leaf L2 is instructed to hunt. The Bitcoin example escapes only because its motive claim targets an INSTITUTION: c-reserve-was-the-product is falsified by 'a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count', which is genuinely checkable because a government has a balance sheet. Point the same tier at a named individual — 'the consultancies sold decomposition because decomposition sells engagements' — and the honest falsifier is a state of mind, and there isn't one.
findings.refuter_pass: Does the falsifier requirement already constrain it adequately, as the brief asks? No, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of care: the tier's own definition and the falsifier requirement cannot both be satisfied for a motive claim about a person. The Bitcoin instance is not a counter-example, it is the boundary case that shows where the tier is safe — institutions, not individuals. Is this MY finding? Honestly, no: my exposure bar is low and being wrong here costs me an angry comment thread, which I said I want. I file it because the mechanism is general and I expect the fraud, geopolitics and entertainment seats to hit it with real exposure — flagged for convergence. Lens or content? Content — one naming rule on one tier.
findings.l2_priority: For any conclusion at far or unhinged naming a living person, score the falsifier as checkable/uncheckable. Convergence expected with public-co-fraud, corruption and electoral seats.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: Briefing is reachable through a subject-new / viewer-new ambiguity, and its honesty obligations make a wrongly-selected Briefing score well
findings.expected: A test in the Briefing entry separating 'the SUBJECT is new' from 'the VIEWER has no position', because a standing argument in front of a new audience satisfies the second and not the first. Ideally the same disqualifier the reference notebook applied by hand — 'no news event; this is a standing condition' — written into the catalogue rather than re-derived per run.
findings.got: 'Use when the subject is new and the viewer has no position yet' (:119), with the two conditions joined and no test to separate them. The trap is sharpened by E's distinctive obligations (:128-130: must be dated, must disclose exposure, must contain a move against its own enthusiasm), which sound like rigour — so a Briefing that should never have been selected passes every honesty signal the methodic checks while producing the competent unwatchable explainer this Creator names as his worst failure mode. engine_fit.why is free text (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:81), so nothing catches the misread. E's closing beat, 'what to do about it', has no honest answer for a six-year architectural argument that is not consultancy advice.
findings.refuter_pass: Marked uncertain deliberately. The disqualifier IS derivable — the reference run derived it correctly and unprompted, recording briefing as 'poor: no news event. This is a standing condition' — so a competent execution plausibly produces the right answer anyway, which is the exact refutation the rubric tells me to try and which I cannot dismiss. What I can say is that the correct reading was re-derived per run rather than read off the catalogue, and that the failure mode when it goes wrong is invisible to every check the methodic runs. That is a discoverability finding against engines, not a demonstrated defect. Lens or content? Content — one clarifying sentence.
findings.l2_priority: Have the run assess engine_fit for briefing without hinting. If it selects or rates briefing 'good', confirmed; if it derives the standing-condition disqualifier unaided as run 1 did, refuted and closed.

findings.creator: software-eng
findings.topic: Microservices went from default advice to cautionary tale in six years, on the same evidence
findings.title: No arbitration when five or more engines fit, and a high engine count is read as a shapeless notebook when it can mean an argument-shaped topic
findings.expected: A tie-break in the Choosing table for the case where many engines fit, and an acknowledgement that engine plurality has two different causes — a notebook with no shape, and a topic that is an ARGUMENT rather than an EVENT. Arguments render many ways by nature; events do not.
findings.got: A one-to-one mapping from 'the idea is...' to an engine (:162-171) plus a note that engines compose, and no guidance when four or five rows fit at once. Six of seven engines render this topic well and the notebook has a very clear shape, so the standing heuristic that a high count is a smell would mislabel it.
findings.refuter_pass: Weakest finding in the set and scored accordingly. The 'seven is a smell' heuristic lives in the skill, not in ENGINES.md, so I may be indicting the catalogue for a rule it never made — hence uncertain, and hence targeting the Choosing table's missing tie-break rather than the heuristic itself. Is it my topic being hard? It is my topic being EASY, which is a novel complaint and I am suspicious of it. Lens or content? Content.
findings.l2_priority: Record how many engines the run rates good-or-better and whether it recommends one with a stated reason or hedges across several.
